claim: Climbing fibers generate complex spikes and Ca2+ transients in cerebellar Purkinje cells, serving as instructive signals.
source: Climbing fibers (CFs) generate complex spikes (CS) and Ca2+ transients in cerebellar Purkinje cells (PCs), serving as instructive signals.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that represents established knowledge in the field about CF function.

claim: The 'all-or-none' character of complex spikes has been questioned since the CF burst was described.
source: The so-called 'all-or-none' character of CSs has been questioned since the CF burst was described.
evidence: This statement references the historical questioning of the all-or-none property based on prior descriptions of CF bursts.

claim: Recent studies have indicated a sensory-driven enhancement of PC Ca2+ signals.
source: Although recent studies have indicated a sensory-driven enhancement of PC Ca2+ signals, how CF responds to sensory events and contributes to PC dendritic Ca2+ and CS remains unexplored.
evidence: This statement refers to recent studies showing sensory-driven enhancement, supported by citations in the field.

claim: The presynaptic CF Ca2+ amplitude encoded the sensory input's strength.
source: Here, single or simultaneous Ca2+ imaging of CFs and PCs in awake mice revealed the presynaptic CF Ca2+ amplitude encoded the sensory input's strength and directly influenced post-synaptic PC dendritic Ca2+ amplitude.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study based on experimental Ca2+ imaging data.

claim: The presynaptic CF Ca2+ amplitude directly influenced post-synaptic PC dendritic Ca2+ amplitude.
source: Here, single or simultaneous Ca2+ imaging of CFs and PCs in awake mice revealed the presynaptic CF Ca2+ amplitude encoded the sensory input's strength and directly influenced post-synaptic PC dendritic Ca2+ amplitude.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study based on experimental Ca2+ imaging data.

claim: The sensory-driven variability in CF Ca2+ amplitude depended on the number of spikes in the CF burst.
source: The sensory-driven variability in CF Ca2+ amplitude depended on the number of spikes in the CF burst.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study based on experimental data.

claim: The spike number of the CF burst determined the PC Ca2+ influx and CS properties.
source: Finally, the spike number of the CF burst determined the PC Ca2+ influx and CS properties.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study based on experimental data.

claim: Each Purkinje cell receives strong excitatory inputs from the inferior olive through a single climbing fiber.
source: Each Purkinje cell (PC), the sole cerebellar output neuron, receives strong excitatory inputs from the inferior olive (IO) through a single climbing fiber (CF), which innervates several PCs (Eccles et al., 1966).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Eccles et al., 1966.

claim: During cerebellar learning, the CF fires in response to unexpected sensory events to provide instructive signals to the PC.
source: During cerebellar learning, the CF fires in response to unexpected sensory events to provide instructive signals to the PC, turning on Ca2+ mediated plasticity mechanisms (Hansel and Linden, 2000; Rancz and Häusser, 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hansel and Linden, 2000 and Rancz and Häusser, 2006.

claim: CF firing turns on Ca2+ mediated plasticity mechanisms in PCs.
source: During cerebellar learning, the CF fires in response to unexpected sensory events to provide instructive signals to the PC, turning on Ca2+ mediated plasticity mechanisms (Hansel and Linden, 2000; Rancz and Häusser, 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hansel and Linden, 2000 and Rancz and Häusser, 2006.

claim: According to the Marr–Albus–Ito theory of learning, a CF-induced PC complex spike response is 'all-or-none'.
source: According to the Marr–Albus–Ito theory of learning, a CF-induced PC complex spike (CS) response is 'all-or-none' because IO stimulation generates seemingly binary responses in the PC (De Schutter and Maex, 1996; Marr, 1969).
evidence: This statement references the Marr-Albus-Ito theory and is supported by citations.

claim: A single CF stimulation induces similar EPSC above a certain stimulus intensity in slice studies.
source: This notion has been prevailed as slice studies have show that a single CF stimulation induces similar EPSC (excitatory post-synaptic current) above a certain stimulus intensity (Konnerth et al., 1990) and is enough to induce parallel fiber (PF)-PC synapse long-term depression (LTD) (Ito and Kano, 1982), in which the level of learning is determined by the range of PF excitation (Reynolds and Hartell, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Konnerth et al., 1990.

claim: A single CF stimulation is enough to induce parallel fiber-PC synapse long-term depression.
source: This notion has been prevailed as slice studies have show that a single CF stimulation induces similar EPSC (excitatory post-synaptic current) above a certain stimulus intensity (Konnerth et al., 1990) and is enough to induce parallel fiber (PF)-PC synapse long-term depression (LTD) (Ito and Kano, 1982), in which the level of learning is determined by the range of PF excitation (Reynolds and Hartell, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ito and Kano, 1982.

claim: The level of learning is determined by the range of PF excitation.
source: This notion has been prevailed as slice studies have show that a single CF stimulation induces similar EPSC (excitatory post-synaptic current) above a certain stimulus intensity (Konnerth et al., 1990) and is enough to induce parallel fiber (PF)-PC synapse long-term depression (LTD) (Ito and Kano, 1982), in which the level of learning is determined by the range of PF excitation (Reynolds and Hartell, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Reynolds and Hartell, 2000.

claim: CF input could critically affect PF-PC LTD by controlling the Ca2+ transient in PC.
source: This means that the CF's impact has little variation in strength and does not carry quantitative information, although CF input, by controlling the Ca2+ transient in PC, could critically affect PF-PC LTD (Ohtsuki et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ohtsuki et al., 2009.

claim: The magnitude of learning is affected by how many invariant CFs synchronously fire.
source: Instead, it is generally accepted that the magnitude of learning is affected by how many invariant CFs synchronously fire (Squire, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Squire, 2009.

claim: The CF's bursting properties have been described.
source: However, the so-called 'all-or-none' property of CF error signal becomes questionable when it comes to in vivo conditions, since the CF's bursting properties have been described (Mathy et al., 2009) and a single non-burst stimulation of CF failed to induce associative learning (Rasmussen et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Mathy et al., 2009.

claim: A single non-burst stimulation of CF failed to induce associative learning.

claim: Longer CS duration was associated with enhanced cerebellar motor learning.
